title: Three years of Neustadt
text: Three budget years of the district around Bf Neustadt, with six roles at three rhythms. Each year the budget committee's rapporteur adopts the rail budget (a turn); the asset manager plans maintenance, renewals and the emergency teams with the district's share of it, and the transport authority's contract manager sets the period's terms (a turn); then a morning at Bf Neustadt is played (a shift): the signaller, the maintenance dispatcher and the undertaking's operations control work with what the plans left them: the teams on shift, assets whose condition decides whether the signal fails, the contract's penalties. The morning's reports go into the year's accounts: the faults of the year times the minutes one fault cost that morning; the undertaking's cancelled and late trains into the contract's incident list. Take the asset manager's seat and let the computer play the others, or share the seats.

phases.title: The night session: the rail budget

debrief: Follow one decision down: what did the asset manager's staff plan change for the maintenance dispatcher that morning, and what did the morning's repair time change in the year's delay minutes?
Follow one result up: what did the rapporteur learn from the district's account, and what did the next budget do with it?
The signal failed and RB 33 left late. Whose sphere was that in the contract's incident list, and who paid?
A morning is a sample of its year. Where would one unlucky morning mislead the people who decide for years?
Which of the six roles had the most to decide, and which had the most effect?
